data.summary: The plan builds a strong foundation in core calculus concepts while prioritizing the student’s weak units (7 and 8) early on. Each week balances new topic study, targeted practice tasks, and live class participation when available. The final week is dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to solidify knowledge before the exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce limits and basic differentiation fundamentals.
tasks: Watch a short video on limit definitions and complete 5 limit‑evaluation problems.
Do 10 derivative‑definition problems (average to instantaneous rate) and check answers with the guide.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of limit properties and the power rule.

weeks.focus: Practice limits, continuity, and power rule applications.
tasks: Estimate limits from graphs and tables for 8 items; verify with algebraic methods.
Complete 12 power‑rule derivative problems, marking each against the solution key.
Write a brief explanation of how continuity relates to differentiability.

weeks.focus: Begin differential equations unit and attend live class.
tasks: Review class notes from live session on modeling with differential equations.
Solve 6 modeling problems (set up DEs) and verify solutions using substitution.
Practice the chain rule on 8 composite‑function derivatives.
Do 5 implicit differentiation problems and check work.

weeks.focus: Expand DE skills and start applications of integration.
tasks: Sketch slope fields for 4 given DEs and describe solution behavior.
Verify solutions for 4 DEs using differentiation.
Calculate average values of 5 functions on given intervals.
Integrate velocity functions to find position; complete 4 problems.

weeks.focus: Contextual and analytical applications of differentiation.
tasks: Interpret derivative meaning in 5 real‑world scenarios.
Solve 4 related‑rates problems (including motion contexts).
Apply the Mean Value Theorem to 3 functions and record conclusions.
Identify critical points and classify them using the First Derivative Test for 5 functions.

weeks.focus: Further analytical differentiation and begin integration fundamentals.
tasks: Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 6 functions.
Use the First Derivative Test to locate local extrema for 5 functions.
Explore accumulation of change by completing 4 accumulation‑function problems.
Approximate areas with Riemann sums for 5 regions using left, right, and midpoint methods.

weeks.focus: Integration techniques and applications, reinforce DE concepts.
tasks: Write definite integrals using summation notation for 4 examples.
Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate 6 integrals.
Solve 5 applied‑integration problems (area between curves, accumulation).
Review DE modeling by re‑solving 2 earlier problems with a different method.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice for all units.
tasks: Take a 90‑minute timed practice exam covering all units; mark using the scoring guide.
Review every incorrect answer, re‑doing the problem with full solution steps.
Complete a mixed‑topic flashcard drill: 2 limit, 2 derivative, 2 integral, 2 DE, 2 application questions.
Finalize a one‑page cheat sheet summarizing key formulas and strategies.

data.final_week_advice: Use the timed practice to identify any lingering weak spots, then spend any remaining study time reviewing those specific problem types. Keep a calm mindset, get plenty of rest the night before the exam, and trust the systematic preparation you’ve built over the past eight weeks.
